title: Impact of Exposure to Persistent Organic Pollutants During Pregnancy on the Composition of Breast Milk and Consequences on the Newborn
brief_summary: Epidemiological studies link early exposure to persistent organic pollutants (POPs) with health consequences in the newborn. Experimental studies have shown the impact of POPs on the gut microbiota. This project aims to characterize the POPs content in breast milk in an exposed population and to evaluate the impact on breast milk composition and intestinal microbiota establishment in the newborn. The health consequences will be evaluated by the clinical follow-up of the newborn.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* newborn born before 33 weeks of amenorrhea or at term born at least 37 weeks of amenorrhea
* mother aged of 18 to 42 years old at the time of inclusion
* mother not deprived of parental rights
* signed concerned consent
* mother having lived for at least 6 months in the Picardie subregion

Exclusion Criteria:

* newborn whose term of birth is between 33 and 37 weeks of amenorrhea
* mother minor or aged over 42 years
* mother deprived of her parental rights
